items.title: Creation
items.summary: The Bible begins with a world called into being by God. Light breaks into darkness; seas, land, plants, stars and living creatures take their places. Humanity is created in God's image and entrusted with the care of creation. The seventh day becomes a day of rest and blessing.
items.lesson: Creation is a gift, not merely a resource to consume. Every person has dignity, and the world deserves careful stewardship.
items.prayer: Creator God, teach me to honour every person and care for the world You have entrusted to us.

items.title: Noah and the Ark
items.summary: Genesis describes a world wounded by violence. Noah listens to God and builds an ark. After the flood, the waters recede, life begins again, and God establishes a covenant with Noah and every living creature. The rainbow becomes its sign.
items.lesson: Hope includes responsibility: protect life, keep promises, and help rebuild after disaster.
items.prayer: God of the covenant, make me faithful in small things and generous in caring for life.

items.title: God Calls Abraham
items.summary: God calls Abram to leave familiar surroundings and travel toward a land he has not yet seen. The promise seems larger than anything he can control, yet Abram sets out. His journey becomes a story of trust, uncertainty and a covenant meant to bless all nations.
items.lesson: Faith often begins with the next faithful step, not a complete map of the future.
items.prayer: God, help me trust You one step at a time and make my life a blessing to others.

items.title: Joseph Forgives His Brothers
items.summary: Joseph is betrayed by his brothers and carried far from home. Years later, after hardship and unexpected responsibility in Egypt, he meets them again. He has the power to take revenge, but instead he provides for the family and recognises that God can bring good even from human wrongdoing.
items.lesson: Forgiveness does not call betrayal good. It refuses to let revenge decide the future and can make room for truth, repair and mercy.
items.prayer: Lord, help me seek what is just without becoming ruled by bitterness. Give me courage to forgive wisely.

items.title: Moses and the Burning Bush
items.summary: While tending sheep, Moses notices a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name and tells him that the suffering of the Israelites has not gone unseen. Moses is sent to confront Pharaoh, despite his doubts, with the promise that God will be with him.
items.lesson: Compassion notices suffering; courage answers the call even when we feel unready.
items.prayer: God who hears the cries of the oppressed, show me one practical way to help someone in need.

items.title: The Exodus and the Red Sea
items.summary: After generations of slavery, the Israelites leave Egypt. When the sea blocks their path and Pharaoh's army approaches, fear rises among the people. The biblical story tells how God makes a way through the sea and leads them toward freedom. Their journey will still require patience, trust and learning.
items.lesson: Freedom is a gift and a responsibility. After leaving what harms us, we must learn to live in justice and care for one another.
items.prayer: God of freedom, guide people who are oppressed and help me work for dignity and peace.

items.title: The Ten Commandments
items.summary: At Mount Sinai, God gives Moses commandments for a people learning to live as a covenant community. The commandments teach Israel to worship God faithfully and to respect life, family, truth, relationships and the goods of others.
items.lesson: Love of God and neighbour belongs together. Faith should shape the way we treat people every day.
items.prayer: Lord, shape my choices so that my worship is joined to honesty, justice and love.

items.title: Ruth Stays with Naomi
items.summary: After loss leaves Naomi grieving and uncertain, Ruth chooses not to abandon her. She travels with Naomi to Bethlehem and works to provide for them. Through the kindness of Boaz and the courage of both women, the family finds security and hope. Ruth becomes part of the family line of David.
items.lesson: Faithfulness often looks like ordinary loyalty, practical help and staying beside someone who is hurting.
items.prayer: God of kindness, help me be present to people who feel alone and serve them with respect.

items.title: Samuel Hears God's Call
items.summary: Young Samuel hears his name called during the night but does not immediately understand. Eli helps him recognise the call, and Samuel answers, 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.' Samuel grows into a prophet who speaks God's word to Israel.
items.lesson: Listening is a spiritual practice. Quiet, Scripture and wise guidance can help us discern what is good.
items.prayer: Lord, quiet my heart enough to listen and give me courage to respond.

items.title: David and Goliath
items.summary: The Israelite army is frightened by Goliath's challenge. David, still young and accustomed to caring for sheep, trusts God and steps forward with a sling and stones rather than heavy armour. The story celebrates courage rooted in faith rather than outward appearance or military power.
items.lesson: Courage is not boasting or pretending danger is small. It is doing what is right with the gifts and help available to us.
items.prayer: God, help me face difficult tasks with humility, preparation and trust.

items.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
items.summary: When God invites Solomon to ask for a gift, Solomon asks for an understanding heart so he can govern the people justly. The story of the two women and the child shows wisdom seeking truth and protecting the vulnerable rather than simply winning an argument.
items.lesson: Wisdom asks what will help people flourish, especially those who have little power.
items.prayer: Lord, give me an understanding heart and help me make fair decisions.

items.title: Elijah and the Still Small Voice
items.summary: Exhausted and afraid, Elijah travels into the wilderness and asks God for help. He receives food and rest before continuing. At Horeb, wind, earthquake and fire pass, but Elijah encounters God in a quiet, gentle sound. He learns that he is not alone.
items.lesson: Rest is not failure. Sometimes we need nourishment, quiet and companionship before we can see the next step.
items.prayer: God of gentle presence, meet me in my weariness and help me receive the care I need.

items.title: Jonah Learns About Mercy
items.summary: Jonah tries to flee from God's call to Nineveh. After a storm and a great fish, he finally delivers the message. The people repent, and God shows mercy. Jonah becomes angry that mercy has reached people he dislikes, revealing how difficult it can be to want compassion for everyone.
items.lesson: God's mercy can challenge our prejudice. It asks us to hope for conversion rather than another person's ruin.
items.prayer: Merciful God, widen my heart and help me desire healing even for people I find difficult.

items.title: Esther's Courage
items.summary: When the Jewish people face danger, Esther is urged to approach the king even though doing so carries risk. She prepares carefully, speaks at the right moment and helps expose the plan against her people. Her courage protects a community threatened by injustice.
items.lesson: Courage can mean using influence to protect people who are vulnerable, even when silence would be easier.
items.prayer: God of justice, give me wisdom and courage to speak up for others.

items.title: The Birth of Jesus
items.summary: Mary receives the angel's message with faith, and Joseph accepts his responsibility in a confusing situation. Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger. Shepherds hear the announcement and come to see the child. The Gospel presents God's glory arriving not in worldly power but in humility.
items.lesson: God often meets us in humble places. Make room for Christ through kindness, hospitality and trust.
items.prayer: Jesus, be welcome in my life. Help me notice Your presence in people the world overlooks.

items.title: The Baptism of Jesus
items.summary: Jesus comes to John at the Jordan. As Jesus is baptised, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice declares him the beloved Son. The scene introduces Jesus' public ministry and reveals his identity before his works begin.
items.lesson: Our worth begins in God's love. Christian service grows from receiving that love, not from trying to earn it.
items.prayer: Father, help me live as Your beloved child and follow Jesus with a willing heart.

items.title: Jesus Calls the First Disciples
items.summary: Jesus meets fishermen at work and calls them to follow him. Simon, Andrew, James and John leave their nets and begin a new journey. They will misunderstand, learn, fail and grow as they travel with Jesus.
items.lesson: Discipleship begins in ordinary life and slowly changes our priorities, relationships and use of our gifts.
items.prayer: Jesus, call me to follow You in the ordinary moments of this day.

items.title: The Wedding at Cana
items.summary: At a wedding in Cana, the wine runs short and the hosts face embarrassment. Mary brings the need to Jesus and tells the servants to do whatever he says. Jesus turns water into wine, and the sign reveals his glory to the disciples.
items.lesson: Notice practical needs around you. Quiet service can protect someone's dignity and become a sign of love.
items.prayer: Jesus, help me notice the needs others may be afraid to mention and serve with generosity.

items.title: The Good Samaritan
items.summary: A traveller is attacked and left wounded. A priest and a Levite pass by, but a Samaritan stops, tends the man's wounds and pays for his care. Jesus turns the question from 'Who counts as my neighbour?' to the challenge of becoming a neighbour through mercy.
items.lesson: Compassion crosses boundaries. Love becomes real when we stop, notice and help wisely.
items.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to people in need and give me the courage to become a neighbour.

items.title: The Lost Sheep
items.summary: Jesus describes a shepherd who searches for one lost sheep while the others remain safe. When the shepherd finds it, he carries it home rejoicing. The parable reveals God's concern for each person and the joy of reconciliation.
items.lesson: No one should be treated as disposable. Seek out people who have been left behind and welcome those who return.
items.prayer: Good Shepherd, help me care for those who feel forgotten and rejoice when someone begins again.

items.title: The Prodigal Son
items.summary: A younger son demands his inheritance, leaves home and wastes it. When hunger and shame bring him to his senses, he returns expecting to be treated as a servant. His father runs to welcome him. The older brother struggles with resentment, and the parable invites both sons into the father's joy.
items.lesson: Receiving mercy can be difficult, and so can celebrating mercy given to someone else. God invites us all into reconciliation.
items.prayer: Father, help me return when I fail, forgive as I have been forgiven, and rejoice in another person's new beginning.

items.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
items.summary: A storm rises while Jesus and the disciples are crossing the lake. The disciples panic and wake Jesus, who commands the wind and sea to be still. He asks about their faith, and they wonder who he is. The story does not deny fear; it brings fear into the presence of Jesus.
items.lesson: Faith does not mean never being afraid. It means bringing fear to God and seeking help rather than facing everything alone.
items.prayer: Lord Jesus, meet me in frightening moments and help me take the next wise step.

items.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
items.summary: A large crowd follows Jesus, and the disciples cannot see how to feed everyone. A boy's five barley loaves and two fish are brought forward. Jesus gives thanks and distributes the food; everyone eats and leftovers are gathered. The sign points beyond scarcity toward God's abundance.
items.lesson: A small gift can become part of a greater good when it is shared. Do not underestimate what you can offer.
items.prayer: Jesus, make me generous with what I have and attentive to people who are hungry.

items.title: The Transfiguration
items.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a mountain to pray. His appearance changes, Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice tells the disciples to listen to God's chosen Son. The moment of glory strengthens them for the difficult road toward Jerusalem.
items.lesson: Moments of clarity should lead us back to faithful daily life, not away from the needs of others.
items.prayer: Father, help me listen to Jesus and carry His light into ordinary life.

items.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
items.summary: During the supper, Jesus rises, wraps a towel around himself and washes his disciples' feet. Peter resists, but Jesus explains that they must receive his service and follow his example. The Lord takes the place of a servant and gives his disciples a pattern for leadership.
items.lesson: Greatness in Jesus' way is measured by service, not status. Let love become practical.
items.prayer: Jesus, teach me to serve without seeking praise and to receive help with humility.

items.title: The Empty Tomb
items.summary: Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb and finds it open. She weeps, not yet understanding what has happened. Then Jesus calls her by name, and she recognises him. She becomes a witness to the Resurrection and carries the news to the disciples.
items.lesson: Christian hope does not pretend grief is unreal. It trusts that the risen Christ can meet us even in sorrow.
items.prayer: Risen Jesus, call me by name and help me carry hope to others.

items.title: The Road to Emmaus
items.summary: Two disciples leave Jerusalem grieving and confused. A stranger walks with them and explains the Scriptures, but they recognise Jesus only when he breaks bread. They return to Jerusalem with renewed hope and news for the others.
items.lesson: Christ can accompany us before we recognise him. Scripture, hospitality and shared worship can open our eyes.
items.prayer: Risen Lord, walk with me, open the Scriptures to my heart and renew my hope.

items.title: Pentecost
items.summary: The disciples gather in prayer when a sound like a strong wind fills the house. Tongues like fire rest upon them, and they begin speaking in different languages. Visitors from many places hear the mighty works of God in their own tongues.
items.lesson: The Holy Spirit gives courage to witness and helps people cross barriers of language and culture.
items.prayer: Holy Spirit, strengthen me to speak with love and welcome people from every nation.
